review_method: manual contact-sheet review of generated outputs

runs.notes: Captured the green pack, phone UI, city/product proof language, and collage structure, but looked more like a rough animatic. UI/text and layout consistency were weak.
Best overall result. Clean cinematic city launch, readable product/app transformation, and convincing checkout proof. Fictional app text still needs controlled overlay work before final production.
Strongest continuity from the source keyframe and good neon reward motion, but less successful as a multi-beat montage. Better suited for single-shot product launch moments.
Variant drifted into a presenter/product-pack ad with fake app text. Less faithful to the Cero montage than the longer primary prompt, but usable as cheap broad social-ad ideation.
Coherent premium product/payment sequence, but it lost the city-launch beat and turned the pack identity into a lime/card motif. Useful commercially, not the closest recreation.
Excellent opening-hook result. Preserved the reference composition, neon pack, city perspective, and upward motion with controlled particles. Current default for launch-hook shots.
Visually strong alternate direction, but shifted into a night sci-fi pack launch. Good for exploratory mood variations, weak for faithful brand-style recreation.
Cleanest proof shot. Strong reference continuity, natural checkout setting, stable phone framing, and clear payment interaction. Needs deterministic UI overlay replacement.
Decent generic contactless-payment shot, but it lost the rewards-app identity and neon-lime brand language. Useful as a cheap generic checkout baseline.

Coherent low-cost product/app scene with clean lime styling, but it ignored the multi-beat montage and stayed in one tabletop setup. Useful for cheap static product-app explorations, not montage reconstruction.
